question.text:
Among the two statements

$(\mathrm{S} 1):(p \Rightarrow q) \wedge(p \wedge(\sim q))$ is a contradiction and

$(\mathrm{S}2) : (p \wedge q) \vee((\sim p) \wedge q) \vee(p \wedge(\sim q)) \vee((\sim p) \wedge(\sim q))$ is a tautology

  1. both are false.
  2. only (S1) is true.
  3. both are true.
  4. only (S2) is true.
question.subject: Artificial Intelligence

question.text:
Equivalent logical expression for the Well Formed Formula $(W F F)$,

$$
\sim(\forall x) F[x]
$$

is

  1. $\forall x(\sim F[x])$
     
  2. $\sim(\exists x) F[x]$
     
  3. $\exists x(\sim F[x])$
     
  4. $\forall x F[x]$

  1. $P \leftrightarrow eg Q$
     
  2. $ eg P \leftrightarrow Q$
     
  3. $ eg P \leftrightarrow eg Q$
     
  4. $Q ightarrow P$

question.text:
The resolvent of the set of clauses $(A \vee B, \sim A \vee D, C \vee \sim B)$ is

  1. $A \vee B$
     
  2. $C \vee D$
     
  3. $A \vee C$
     
  4. $A \vee D$

question.text:

  1. $(\sim(p \wedge q)) \wedge q$
     
  2. $(\sim(p \wedge q)) \vee p$
     
  3. $p \vee q$
